en.biologicalProcess: Stem internodes elongate through rapid cellular division in intercalary meristems located just above each stem node.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Tillering allows a single seed to produce multiple grain-bearing heads, dynamically compensating for sparse planting density.
en.environmentalInfluences: Adequate nitrogen and moisture stimulate robust tiller survival; severe drought causes secondary tillers to abort.

en.title: Booting & Swelling Flag Sheath
en.shortSummary: Flag leaf sheath swells as the immature spike develops internally.
en.script: Inside the uppermost leaf sheath—the flag leaf—the reproductive spike is developing. The sheath swells prominently in the booting stage, concealing and protecting the developing spikelets from temperature shocks.
en.script2x: During the boot stage, the developing wheat spike swells inside the sheath of the uppermost flag leaf.
en.script5x: Booting Stage: Swelling spike head is held within the protective flag leaf sheath.
en.visualChanges: The upper stem thickens into a swollen green cigar-shaped sheath directly below the broad, arching flag leaf.
en.biologicalProcess: Meiosis takes place inside developing anthers and ovaries within the spikelets while the flag leaf provides over fifty percent of grain-filling carbohydrates.
en.ecologicalSignificance: The flag leaf is the engine of wheat yield, ideally positioned to intercept maximum overhead sunlight.
en.environmentalInfluences: Extreme heat or water stress during booting disrupts meiosis, causing pollen sterility and unfertilized heads.

en.title: Heading & Spike Anthesis
en.shortSummary: Bearded spike emerges from flag leaf; yellow anthers extrude.
en.script: The majestic wheat spike emerges from the flag leaf, brandishing long protective awns. Tiny glumes open briefly to extrude delicate yellow anthers, releasing clouds of pollen to self-fertilize each floret within minutes.
en.script2x: The spike emerges and tiny florets open for anthesis, exposing feathery stigmas and pale yellow anthers.
en.script5x: Heading & Anthesis: Wheat ear emerges and florets open for pollination.
en.visualChanges: Bristly bearded spike fully emerges atop the tall culm; tiny pale-yellow stamens dangle along the spikelets.
en.biologicalProcess: Wheat is predominantly cleistogamous, achieving rapid self-pollination before the glumes open to the open atmosphere.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Rapid self-pollination insulates the plant from dependence on wind direction or insect pollinators during critical bloom.
en.environmentalInfluences: Hot, dry winds during anthesis desicate delicate stigmas; moderate temperatures around 20 degrees Celsius optimize seed set.

en.title: Watery Ripe Kernel Set

en.script2x: Wheat flowers self-pollinate swiftly within the glumes via wind currents and gravity.
en.script5x: Wind Pollination: Rapid self-pollination takes place inside protective glumes.
en.visualChanges: Anthers dry up; individual spikelets feel firm as tiny, translucent green kernels form inside the protective husks.
en.biologicalProcess: Rapid cellular division within the syncytial endosperm creates thousands of cell compartments ready to store starch granules.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Spikelet awns act as photosynthetic appendages, providing localized carbon capture right next to the developing grain sink.
en.environmentalInfluences: Water deficit at this juncture limits the ultimate number of endosperm cells, capping the maximum potential grain weight.

en.title: Milk Development Stage
en.shortSummary: Endosperm turns milky white as starch accumulates rapidly.
en.script: The grain enters the milk stage. When crushed, the kernel yields a rich milky-white fluid packed with starch granules and gluten proteins transferred from the senescing lower canopy into the spike.

en.biologicalProcess: Sucrose imported through the vascular crease is enzymatically converted into amylose and amylopectin starch by starch synthases.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Wheat concentrates massive carbohydrate and protein reserves into a compact seed to survive dry grassland environments.
en.environmentalInfluences: High temperatures above 30 degrees Celsius shorten the milk filling period, causing pinched, lightweight grain.

en.title: Soft to Hard Dough Stage
en.shortSummary: Kernel turns doughy and firm; awns and spikelets yellow.
en.script: The kernel transitions from soft to hard dough. Starch solidifies, chlorophyll fades from the leaves and stem, and the entire wheat plant transforms from deep green into a shimmering sea of golden amber.
en.script2x: Stems and ears lose moisture, transitioning from lush green to a radiant shimmering golden amber.
en.script5x: Ripening: Moisture drops and fields turn to shimmering golden amber.
en.visualChanges: Foliage and stems turn pale yellow; kernels lose milky fluid, becoming firm and compressible like bread dough.
en.biologicalProcess: Rapid loss of kernel water triggers protein matrix consolidation, binding glutenin and gliadin polymers around starch granules.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Progressive desiccation prepares the embryo for long-term dormancy through dry Mediterranean or continental winters.
en.environmentalInfluences: Rain during late dough stages can trigger premature sprouting on the spike, damaging grain quality.

en.title: Golden Hard Grain Harvest
en.shortSummary: Golden amber wheat spike with hard dry kernels and bowing stem.
en.script: The golden harvest has arrived. The wheat spike bows gracefully under the weight of its hard, dry caryopsis grains. The straw is dry and rustling, ready for threshing and carrying humanity’s ancient breadbasket forward.
en.script2x: Golden wheat heads bow heavily under the weight of hard, mature grains, ready for combine harvest.
en.script5x: Full Maturity: Hard, dry golden grains in bowed heads ready for harvest.
en.visualChanges: Uniform golden-amber field with bowing bearded spikes, dry parchment-like husks, and flint-hard mature grains.
en.biologicalProcess: Grain moisture drops below fourteen percent; seed enters profound metabolic dormancy with stable cellular vitrification.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Dry caryopsis can survive years in dry soil or granaries without losing embryo viability or nutritional value.
en.environmentalInfluences: Dry, low-humidity harvest weather preserves grain hardness and prevents fungal mycotoxin accumulation.

en.title: Chilli Seed Imbibition
en.shortSummary: Warm soil temperature triggers enzyme activation in chilli seed.
en.script: Nestled in warm, fertile soil, the pale chilli seed absorbs water through its tough seed coat. Native to the tropical Americas, chilli seeds require deep soil warmth to stir their embryonic metabolism from dormancy.
en.script2x: The flattened pepper seed absorbs soil moisture, activating internal gibberellins to dissolve stored endosperm.
en.script5x: Seed Imbibition: Warm moisture activates stored reserves within the pepper seed.
en.visualChanges: Smooth, cream-colored flat seed swells as moisture permeates its tough outer coat.
en.biologicalProcess: Imbibition rehydrates the embryonic axis and endosperm, triggering hydrolytic enzyme activation for protein mobilization.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Capsaicin in placental tissue of the mother fruit deters mammalian seed chewing while permitting bird dispersal into warm habitats.
en.environmentalInfluences: Chilli seeds demand warm soil temperatures between 24 and 30 degrees Celsius; cold soil below 15 degrees stalls germination completely.

en.title: Lateral Taproot Architecture

en.script: A strong central taproot drives deep into the soil profile, flanked by an extensive network of horizontal feeder roots. This balanced architecture provides both deep water security and rapid access to topsoil warmth and nutrients.

en.biologicalProcess: Auxin gradient maxima in the pericycle layer trigger lateral root primordia emergence through the cortex and epidermis.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Enables adaptation to periodic drought conditions typical of semi-arid tropical scrublands.
en.environmentalInfluences: Compacted clay soils severely restrict lateral spread; well-drained loams optimize root respiration and nutrient uptake.

en.title: Shoot Emergence & Cotyledon Arc
en.shortSummary: Slender hypocotyl lifts narrow cotyledons into the light.
en.script: The slender green hypocotyl arches upward through the topsoil, lifting the seed coat and cotyledons into the sunlight. Upon sensing light, the shoot straightens, shedding its protective hull to open its cotyledons.
en.script2x: The arched green hypocotyl lifts the seedling above ground, shaking off the seed coat as it greets the light.
en.script5x: Shoot Emergence: Hypocotyl lifts the seedling into the light and sheds the husk.
en.visualChanges: Pale green loop emerges through the soil surface, straightening to unfurl two narrow, strap-like green cotyledons.
en.biologicalProcess: Cryptochrome and phytochrome photoreceptors perceive blue and red light, halting elongation and inducing rapid greening.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Swift emergence prevents seed-borne pathogens from attacking tender shoot tissue in warm, humid soil crusts.
en.environmentalInfluences: Requires bright direct sunlight; low light leads to leggy, weak seedlings susceptible to lodging.

hi.title: मिर्च: प्ररोह निकास

hi.script5x: प्ररोह निकास: मिर्च का तना प्रकाश की ओर बाहर निकलता है।

hi.biologicalProcess: मिर्च की आंतरिक कोशिकाएं इस चरण के विशेष कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।

mr.title: मिरची: कोंब बाहेर येणे

en.title: First Pointed True Leaves
en.shortSummary: Glossy ovate true leaves emerge with acuminate tips.
en.script: Above the narrow cotyledons, the first true leaves emerge. Featuring glossy surfaces and elegant pointed drip-tips, these leaves immediately begin manufacturing sugars to accelerate the young plant’s development.
en.script2x: Two lance-shaped cotyledons flatten out, followed by the appearance of shiny, dark green true leaves.
en.script5x: Seedling: Smooth lanceolate cotyledons spread and true leaves expand.
en.visualChanges: Glossy, deep-green ovate leaves emerge with distinct pointed tips, forming a sturdy young seedling.
en.biologicalProcess: Differentiation of photosynthetic mesophyll layers and formation of stomatal complexes on the abaxial leaf surface.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Acuminate drip tips facilitate rapid drainage of rain droplets, preventing fungal spore adhesion in humid climates.
en.environmentalInfluences: Requires ambient temperatures above 20 degrees Celsius; cold drafts can induce foliar purpling and growth stagnation.

hi.script5x: अंकुर अवस्था: मिर्च की पत्तियाँ भोजन बनाने लगती हैं।

mr.shortSummary: मिरचीच्या वाढीचा रोपटे टप्पा टप्पा.

en.title: Dichotomous Branching Canopy
en.shortSummary: Central stem forks repeatedly into a dense, bushy canopy.
en.script: The chilli plant transitions into its signature dichotomous branching habit. The central main stem terminates in a flower bud and forks into two equal lateral shoots, which fork again and again, creating a dense, protective canopy.
en.script2x: The chilli bush develops a characteristic dichotomous branching architecture with dense, glossy foliage.
en.script5x: Vegetative Forking: Stems fork into an open, sturdy bush with glossy green leaves.
en.visualChanges: Main stem forks symmetrically into multiple branching arms, forming a bushy, umbrella-like green canopy.
en.biologicalProcess: Sympodial branching orchestrated by apical dominance release, where each terminal node produces two lateral vegetative branches.
en.ecologicalSignificance: A spreading bushy canopy shields developing fruit below from harsh tropical sunscald.
en.environmentalInfluences: Thrives in warm days around 26 to 28 degrees Celsius, high solar irradiance, and balanced nitrogen and magnesium.

hi.title: मिर्च: वानस्पतिक वृद्धि

mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Rylski (1972) Effect of Early Environment on Flowering and Fruit Set in Sweet Pepper, Journal of the American Society for Horticultural Science.

en.title: Axillary Fork Budding
en.shortSummary: Solitary floral buds form in the axils of branch forks.
en.script: At every fork in the branches, solitary floral buds develop on slender nodding pedicels. Tightly wrapped in pale green sepals, these buds hold the delicate white petals and reproductive organs in safe custody.
en.script2x: Nodding green flower buds appear in the stem axils, hanging on slender, flexible pedicels.
en.script5x: Bud Formation: Inverted floral buds emerge at the branch fork nodes.
en.visualChanges: Small, pendant green buds form at the junction of each stem fork, hanging on graceful curved pedicels.
en.biologicalProcess: Floral transition at the fork apex triggered by day-neutral florigen signaling in mature vegetative leaves.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Continuous branching ensures a prolonged, staggered succession of flowers rather than a single vulnerable bloom window.
en.environmentalInfluences: Night temperatures below 12 degrees or above 24 degrees Celsius induce bud drop; stable nights ensure retention.

en.title: Nodding White Bloom
en.shortSummary: Pendant white blossoms open with bluish-purple anthers.
en.script: Delicate star-like white blossoms unfurl, nodding gracefully downward. Inside, a ring of striking bluish-purple anthers surrounds the central stigma, releasing fine pollen grains that drift inward to ensure self-pollination.
en.script2x: Delicate star-shaped white blossoms open, displaying pale blue-purple anthers loaded with fertile pollen.
en.script5x: Flowering: Starry white flowers open with distinctive purplish-blue anthers.
en.visualChanges: Pendant white flowers with six pointed petals and distinctive bluish-purple anthers facing downward beneath the leaves.
en.biologicalProcess: Self-pollination occurs as anthers dehisce longitudinally, with gravity aiding pollen transfer to the stigma below.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Downward-facing blossoms protect delicate reproductive organs from torrential rainfall and solar UV radiation.
en.environmentalInfluences: High temperatures exceeding 32 degrees Celsius dry out stigmatic fluid, causing poor fertilization and blossom drop.

en.title: Conical Pod Emergence
en.shortSummary: Ovary elongates past persistent calyx into a green conical pod.
en.script: Fertilization succeeds, and the white petals drop away. Anchored by a persistent green calyx cup, the fertilized ovary elongates rapidly into a glossy, pointed green pod, pointing downward toward the soil.
en.script2x: Air movement and visiting insects vibrate the drooping flowers, transferring pollen onto the central stigma.
en.script5x: Pollination: Gentle breeze and pollinators fertilize the nodding blossoms.
en.visualChanges: Petals fall, leaving a small, glossy green conical pepper pod expanding outward from the star-shaped green calyx.
en.biologicalProcess: Endogenous auxin and gibberellin synthesis in fertilized seeds drives rapid cell division in the pod pericarp wall.
en.ecologicalSignificance: The persistent calyx provides structural strength to support the heavy hanging weight of the expanding pod.
en.environmentalInfluences: Inconsistent moisture during fruit set causes blossom-end rot due to localized calcium transport deficiencies.

hi.title: मिर्च: परागण व फल स्थापना

hi.script: सफल परागण के उपरांत पंखुड़ियाँ मुरझा जाती हैं और मिर्च का अंडाशय निषेचित होकर नन्हे फल या बीज का रूप धारण करता है।
hi.script2x: परागण पूर्ण होने पर पुष्प गिरते हैं और नन्हा फल या बीज बनना शुरू होता है।
hi.script5x: फल स्थापना: मिर्च में परागण के बाद बीज व फल बनना शुरू होता है।
hi.visualChanges: मिर्च के आकार और संरचना में स्पष्ट परिवर्तन दिखाई देते हैं।
hi.biologicalProcess: मिर्च की आंतरिक कोशिकाएं इस चरण के विशेष कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।
hi.ecologicalSignificance: यह चरण पौधे की उत्तरजीविता और संतति प्रसार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।
hi.environmentalInfluences: अनुकूल प्रकाश, तापमान और नमी इस चरण को स्वस्थ बनाए रखते हैं।

mr.title: मिरची: परागीभवन व फळधारणा

mr.script2x: परागीभवनानंतर पाकळ्या गळून लहान फळ किंवा बी धरू लागते.
mr.script5x: फळधारणा: मिरचीमध्ये परागीभवनानंतर फळ धरण्यास सुरुवात होते.
mr.visualChanges: मिरचीच्या रचनेत आणि बाह्य आकारात लक्षणीय बदल दिसून येतात.
mr.biologicalProcess: मिरचीच्या पेशी या टप्प्यातील आवश्यक जैविक क्रिया पूर्ण करतात.
mr.ecologicalSignificance: हा टप्पा वनस्पतीचे अस्तित्व आणि वंशवृद्धी टिकवण्यासाठी अत्यंत महत्त्वाचा आहे.
mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Tewksbury & Nabhan (2001) Directed Deterrence by Capsaicin in Chillies, Nature.

en.title: Pod Expansion & Capsaicin Synthesis
en.shortSummary: Chilli pods rapidly lengthen and develop characteristic pungency.
en.script: The chilli pod expands to its full elongated shape. Inside, glandular epidermal cells along the central placenta begin synthesizing capsaicin, loading the interior ribs with fiery heat while the outer skin remains crisp and green.
en.script2x: Fertilized ovaries elongate into glossy green peppers, synthesizing capsaicin in the inner placental ribs.
en.script5x: Fruit Growth: Peppers elongate rapidly, synthesizing pungent capsaicin within.
en.visualChanges: Chilli pods elongate into full-sized, glossy green conical peppers suspended gracefully from sturdy branch nodes.
en.biologicalProcess: Capsaicinoid synthetase combines vanillylamine with branched-chain fatty acids along placental dissepiment glands to produce capsaicin.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Capsaicin causes severe burning pain to mammalian predators while leaving seed-dispersing avian guts completely unaffected.
en.environmentalInfluences: Mild environmental water stress can actually increase capsaicin concentrations without sacrificing overall plant health.

hi.script5x: फल विस्तार: मिर्च का फल या बीज तेजी से पोषण संचित करता है।
hi.visualChanges: मिर्च के आकार और संरचना में स्पष्ट परिवर्तन दिखाई देते हैं।

mr.script5x: फळ वाढ: मिरचीचे फळ किंवा दाणे आकाराने मोठे होतात.

mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Camara et al. (1995) Carotenoid Biosynthesis and Plastid Differentiation in Pepper Fruits.

en.title: Breaker Variegation Shift
en.shortSummary: Chlorophyll fades; carotenoid and capsanthin synthesis shifts pod.
en.script: The chilli enters its dramatic ripening phase. Deep green skin breaks into streaks of chocolate brown, orange, and vibrant scarlet as chlorophyll degrades and the pod synthesizes brilliant red capsanthin pigments.
en.script2x: Chlorophyll breaks down as capsanthin pigments synthesize, turning the green chilli into fiery crimson.
en.script5x: Color Break: Capsanthin synthesis turns peppers from deep green to fiery red.
en.visualChanges: Green pods develop striking streaks of purple, orange, and bright red before turning uniformly scarlet.
en.biologicalProcess: Plastid transition from photosynthetic chloroplasts into pigment-storing chromoplasts rich in capsanthin and capsorubin carotenoids.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Brilliant red coloration is easily detected by birds across long distances against dense green foliage.
en.environmentalInfluences: Warm sunny weather accelerates uniform color transformation; cold spells delay pigment synthesis.

mr.script2x: रंग बदलून आणि दाणे भरून पीक काढणीसाठी परिपक्व बनते.
mr.script5x: पीक पिकणे: मिरचीचे पीक पूर्णपणे पक्व होते.
mr.visualChanges: मिरचीच्या रचनेत आणि बाह्य आकारात लक्षणीय बदल दिसून येतात.

stages.references: Levey et al. (2006) A Chemical Basis for Differential Fruit Consumption by Birds and Mammals, Ecology.

en.title: Fiery Crimson Pods & Seed Maturity
en.shortSummary: Glossy deep-red ripe cayenne chillies suspended from sturdy branches.
en.script: The chilli pepper stands in all its fiery glory. Radiant crimson pods hang proudly from sturdy branches, packed with mature, viable seeds protected by fiery placenta tissues, awaiting dispersal across the landscape.
en.script2x: The bushy chilli plant displays vibrant fiery peppers, bursting with concentrated capsaicin and ready for picking.
en.script5x: Full Maturity: Heavy crop of glossy, fiery hot chillies ready for harvest.
en.visualChanges: Bushy plant laden with dozens of glossy, deep-crimson ripe chilli peppers ready for harvest.
en.biologicalProcess: Complete physiological seed maturity; embryo enters stable dormancy with protective endosperm and full capsaicin matrix.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Birds consume ripe pods whole, dispersing undamaged seeds miles away with their own natural fertilizer packets.
en.environmentalInfluences: Harvesting mature peppers stimulates continued flower and fruit production along newer branch nodes.

stages.references: Vergara (1992) A Farmer’s Primer on Growing Rice, International Rice Research Institute (IRRI).

en.title: Paddy Imbibition
en.shortSummary: Paddy grain hydrates under warm, anaerobic submerged conditions.
en.script: Submerged in the warm, silt-laden water of the paddy, the rough rice grain begins imbibition. Unlike most crops that drown in water, rice possesses specialized genetics allowing it to germinate even under hypoxic conditions.
en.script2x: The submerged paddy seed imbibes water through its fibrous hull, awakening cellular respiration under low oxygen.
en.script5x: Paddy Imbibition: Rice grain imbibes water and initiates aquatic germination.
en.visualChanges: Golden-brown rough rice hull hydrates and swells slightly beneath shallow warm water.
en.biologicalProcess: Alcohol dehydrogenase and fermentative metabolic pathways allow initial ATP generation even under extremely low dissolved oxygen.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Evolutionary adaptation to wetlands and flooded floodplains, outcompeting terrestrial weeds that cannot survive inundation.
en.environmentalInfluences: Optimal water temperature between 25 and 30 degrees Celsius; cold spring water delays germination and invites water molds.

en.title: Coleoptile Sprout
en.shortSummary: Coleoptile emerges upward toward oxygen and light.
en.script: Under water, the rice seed prioritizes vertical shoot escape. A hollow white coleoptile thrusts upward through the water column, acting like a snorkel to reach atmospheric oxygen before substantial root growth begins.

en.script: Deep within the base of the culm, a microscopic branched panicle primordium initiates. Over the coming weeks, it journeys upward through the stem, swelling the flag leaf sheath in the critical booting phase.
en.script2x: Panicle differentiation begins deep within the stem sheath during the swelling boot stage.
en.script5x: Panicle Booting: Developing grain heads swell inside the protective sheath.
en.visualChanges: Stem internodes elongate rapidly; the upper sheath bulges noticeably as the developing grain head prepares to emerge.
en.biologicalProcess: Microscopic inflorescence branching establishes the potential number of spikelets and grains per panicle under genetic control.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Hiding the developing reproductive head inside the water-cooled sheath protects fragile gametes from extreme surface heat.
en.environmentalInfluences: Extremely sensitive to cold spells below 18 degrees or heatwaves above 35 degrees during microsporogenesis, which can cause spikelet sterility.

hi.script5x: कली निर्माण: धान (चावल) पर पुष्प कलियाँ विकसित होती हैं।

en.title: Heading & Morning Anthesis
en.shortSummary: Panicle emerges from flag leaf; glumes open for brief morning anthesis.
en.script: The delicate branched panicle bursts forth from the flag leaf. In the warmth of the morning sun, protective lemma and palea glumes swing open for less than an hour, extruding six yellow stamens to pollinate the feathery stigmas.
en.script2x: The branched panicle emerges above the canopy and spikelets open briefly in the midday warmth for anthesis.
en.script5x: Heading: Arching panicles emerge and tiny white spikelets open to pollinate.
en.visualChanges: Graceful branched panicle stands erect atop the tiller; minute yellow anthers dangle along the spikelets for a brief morning hour.
en.biologicalProcess: Rapid turgor swelling in the lodicule organs pushes the glumes open, allowing wind-mediated self-pollination before glumes snap shut.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Brief morning flowering window minimizes exposure to midday desiccating heat and afternoon monsoon rainstorms.
en.environmentalInfluences: Temperatures above 35 degrees Celsius at anthesis cause anther indehiscence and severe floret sterility.

en.title: Milky Kernel Fill
en.shortSummary: Spikelets fill with milky liquid starch; panicle begins nodding.
en.script: Pollination succeeds, and the fertilized ovary begins to swell. Inside each enclosed spikelet, the developing kernel fills with a sweet, milky liquid starch, and the heavy panicle begins to bow gracefully under its increasing weight.
en.script2x: Rice florets self-pollinate within minutes as breezes transfer pollen grains inside the palea and lemma.
en.script5x: Pollination: Swift self-pollination takes place inside the protective hulls.
en.visualChanges: Spikelets feel plump and firm; green grains yield a white milky fluid when pressed, and the panicle tip curves downward.
en.biologicalProcess: Photosynthates from the flag leaf and green glumes are actively transported via phloem into the endosperm, synthesizing starch granules.
en.ecologicalSignificance: The heavy panicle nods downward into the canopy, reducing wind resistance and lowering the center of gravity.
en.environmentalInfluences: Moderate temperatures and bright sunny days promote maximum photosynthetic efficiency during milk filling.

en.title: Soft Dough Grain Solidification
en.shortSummary: Grain solidifies into soft dough; hulls turn light green-yellow.
en.script: The watery milk solidifies into a soft, chalky dough. The protective lemma and palea husks begin their color transition, fading from bright photosynthetic green to soft straw-yellow as starch crystallization progresses.
en.script2x: Starch fills the developing kernels through milk and dough stages, causing the green panicles to bow downward.
en.script5x: Grain Fill: Kernels fill with starch, weighing down the arching panicles.
en.visualChanges: Panicles bend noticeably lower; grains become solid and dough-like, and hulls lighten from green to pale yellow.
en.biologicalProcess: Starch debranching enzymes and granule-bound starch synthases consolidate amylose and amylopectin into crystalline matrices.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Solidification of the endosperm seals the grain against insect probing and bacterial spoilage.
en.environmentalInfluences: Water management is vital: maintaining a shallow water depth prevents moisture stress while avoiding stagnant waterlogging.

en.title: Hard Dough & Golden Panicle Arc
en.shortSummary: Kernels harden; panicles turn golden yellow and arch downward.
en.script: The grain enters the hard dough stage. Kernels lose moisture, hardening into firm rough rice grains. The panicles arch deeply in golden arcs, while the vegetative canopy begins its natural, orderly golden senescence.
en.script2x: The paddy dries down as the grain moisture drops, turning the emerald canopy into a sea of radiant golden amber.
en.script5x: Ripening: Grains harden and the crop turns from vivid green to rich golden straw.
en.visualChanges: Heads arch into graceful golden bows; rough rice grains feel hard under pressure, and foliage begins yellowing.
en.biologicalProcess: Chlorophyll degradation in lower leaves remobilizes remaining nitrogen and minerals to complete grain maturation.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Bowed panicles position mature grains closer to the soil, facilitating natural seed shed once floodwaters recede.
en.environmentalInfluences: Paddy water is typically drained at this stage to dry the soil surface and encourage uniform grain dry-down.

en.title: Rose Achene Imbibition
en.shortSummary: Rose achene seed softens after a cold stratification period.
en.script: Encased in a tough, bony pericarp, the rose achene rests in cool, damp soil. After enduring months of winter chill—a process known as stratification—the hard shell softens, allowing water to awaken the dormant embryo inside.
en.script2x: The hard rose hip achene absorbs winter moisture, softening its thick shell to break physiological dormancy.
en.script5x: Achene Imbibition: Moisture and cold stratification awaken the dormant rose seed.
en.visualChanges: Hard, angular yellowish-brown seed absorbs moisture, softening along the suture line.
en.biologicalProcess: Cold stratification degrades germination-inhibiting abscisic acid, allowing gibberellins to stimulate cell elongation in the embryonic axis.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Deep dormancy prevents autumn germination, ensuring the fragile seedling emerges only in the forgiving warmth of spring.
en.environmentalInfluences: Requires eight to twelve weeks of moist chilling near 4 degrees Celsius to break physiological embryo dormancy.

en.title: Radicle Anchor
en.shortSummary: A strong taproot descends deeply into the subsoil.
en.script: The bony achene splits at its seam. A resilient white radicle emerges, thrusting decisively downward into the subsoil to establish the deep anchor that will sustain this woody perennial shrub for decades to come.
en.script2x: The primary radicle breaks free from the hard woody shell and anchors downward into the soil.

en.biologicalProcess: Positive gravitropism directs cell expansion downward, laying down the primary vascular cylinder of the future woody taproot.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Woody shrubs require robust early anchoring to withstand wind buffeting and seasonal soil shifting.
en.environmentalInfluences: Deep, well-aerated loam promotes rapid root penetration; standing water creates root rot and halts germination.

en.biologicalProcess: Secondary vascular cambium initiates secondary xylem (wood) and phloem, increasing structural rigidity and transport capacity.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Woody root crowns store massive starch reserves that fuel spring leaf-out and recovery from drought or herbivory.

en.title: First Odd-Pinnate Leaves
en.shortSummary: First odd-pinnate leaf emerges with serrated margins.
en.script: The young cane unfurls its signature foliage: odd-pinnate compound leaves featuring finely serrated margins. Glandular hairs along the leaf margins emit the delicate, sweet apple-like fragrance characteristic of the sweetbriar rose.
en.script2x: Odd-pinnate serrated leaves unfold along the young stem, carrying basal stipules typical of Rosaceae.
en.script5x: Seedling: Classic serrated compound leaves unfold along the juvenile cane.
en.visualChanges: Delicate compound leaves with five serrated leaflets spread open along the slender reddish cane.
en.biologicalProcess: Foliar glandular trichomes synthesize aromatic terpenes and resinous compounds, creating the sweetbriar scent.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Resinous foliar secretions provide chemical deterrence against insect herbivores and fungal spore germination.
en.environmentalInfluences: Requires good air circulation and morning sun to dry leaves quickly and prevent powdery mildew or black spot.

hi.script2x: बीजपत्र फैलते हैं और सच्ची पत्तियाँ सक्रिय प्रकाश संश्लेषण शुरू करती हैं।
hi.script5x: अंकुर अवस्था: गुलाब की पत्तियाँ भोजन बनाने लगती हैं।

en.title: Cane Arching & Dense Foliage
en.shortSummary: Woody canes elongate, branching laterally with dark glossy foliage.
en.script: The rose surges into vigorous perennial growth. Sturdy canes elongate and arch gracefully, lignifying into tough woody stems armed with curved prickles. Glossy compound leaves weave into a dense, sprawling shrub canopy.
en.script2x: Woody canes surge upward and arch outward, forming an impenetrable thorny framework of glossy green leaves.
en.script5x: Vegetative Canes: Sturdy woody canes elongate and branch into a full thorny shrub.
en.visualChanges: Canes thicken, turning from green to woody brown with sharp recurved thorns and dense dark-green compound foliage.
en.biologicalProcess: Vascular cambium continuously lays down dense ring-porous secondary xylem, providing immense mechanical strength.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Recurved prickles act like climbing grappling hooks, allowing the canes to clamber over surrounding shrubs and rocks.
en.environmentalInfluences: Requires full sun of at least six hours daily and balanced nutrition; nitrogen promotes strong basal cane extension.

hi.title: गुलाब: वानस्पतिक वृद्धि

hi.script5x: वानस्पतिक वृद्धि: गुलाब का मजबूत ढाँचा और छत्र विकसित होता है।

en.title: Swelling Urn-Shaped Buds
en.shortSummary: Urn-shaped floral buds form; green sepals begin reflexing.
en.script: At the tips of lateral canes, urn-shaped floral buds swell. Five long, pinnatifid green sepals wrap tightly around the bud, their glandular margins protecting the tightly folded petals within until the flower is ready to open.
en.script2x: Sepals envelope the developing flower bud, which swells at the tip of terminal shoots with tightly folded petals.
en.script5x: Bud Formation: Plump floral buds swell at branch tips, wrapped in green sepals.
en.visualChanges: Pointed green floral buds swell at branch tips, with feathery sepal tips beginning to part.
en.biologicalProcess: Floral transition driven by photoperiodic signals and seasonal thermal accumulation, organizing floral whorls in concentric phyllotaxis.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Pinnatifid glandular sepals secrete sticky resins that trap small thrips and aphids before they can damage inner petals.
en.environmentalInfluences: Dry, warm days promote steady bud development; prolonged cold or rain can cause bud balling, where petals rot before opening.

mr.script5x: कळी धरणे: गुलाबवर फुलांच्या कळ्या दिसू लागतात.

en.title: Corolla Anthesis Bloom
en.shortSummary: Velvety petals unfold in concentric whorls around golden stamens.
en.script: The sepals reflex backward, and velvety petals unfold into a glorious blossom. A central fountain of bright golden stamens stands surrounded by the delicate corolla, filling the garden with sweet, timeless floral fragrance.
en.script2x: Fragrant velvety rose petals unfurl in radiant succession, exposing a golden crown of fertile stamens.
en.script5x: Anthesis: Fragrant velvety rose blossoms unfurl in dramatic splendor.
en.visualChanges: Exquisite multi-petaled rose blossom opens wide, revealing a bright yellow cluster of stamens at its center.
en.biologicalProcess: Petal expansion is driven by localized cellular vacuolation; osmophores on the petal surface volatilize geraniol and citronellol aromas.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Abundant pollen and rich volatile aromas attract a wide diversity of bumblebees, honeybees, and flower beetles.
en.environmentalInfluences: Mild temperatures of 20 to 24 degrees Celsius prolong bloom life; intense scorching heat accelerates petal wilting.

en.title: Peak Bloom & Fragrance
en.shortSummary: Magnificent rose in peak bloom emitting sweet fragrance.
en.script: The blossom reaches its peak presentation. Hovering pollinators gather golden pollen, brushing against the clustered stigmas in the center of the flower cup, ensuring successful cross-fertilization across the multi-ovule hypanthium.
en.script2x: Bees delve into the fragrant blossoms, gathering pollen and transferring grains onto the sticky stigmas.
en.script5x: Pollination: Foraging bees pollinate the dense ring of stigmas at the blossom core.
en.visualChanges: Blossom fully expanded in radiant beauty, with glistening pollen-laden anthers and sweet perfume filling the air.
en.biologicalProcess: Multiple pollen tubes grow down individual styles enclosed inside the urn-shaped hypanthium, fertilizing separate ovules.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Ensures that multiple achenes develop inside the future hip, maximizing the genetic return on floral investment.
en.environmentalInfluences: Calm, sunny days foster high pollinator visitation; heavy rains dislodge pollen and dampen scent dispersion.

mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Nilsson (1967) The Genus Rosa: Cytogenetics and Taxonomy, Hereditas.

en.title: Petal Senescence & Hypanthium Swell
en.shortSummary: Petals mature and drop as hypanthium begins swelling below sepals.
en.script: With pollination complete, the delicate petals senesce and flutter to the ground. Below the reflexed sepals, the urn-shaped hypanthium swells into a firm green vessel, nourishing the developing achene seeds inside its fleshy cup.
en.script2x: Petals fall as the hypanthium receptacle swells into a firm green rose hip encasing developing seeds.
en.script5x: Hip Development: Fleshy hypanthium swells into a green, nutrient-packed rose hip.
en.visualChanges: Petals fall away, leaving the swollen green cup-like hypanthium crowned by drying brown sepals.
en.biologicalProcess: Auxin from fertilized ovules prevents the abscission of the flower receptacle, stimulating flesh proliferation in the hypanthium.
en.ecologicalSignificance: The rose hip is an accessory fruit formed from the floral cup, protecting multiple hard-walled achene seeds within.
en.environmentalInfluences: Consistent soil moisture supports steady hip expansion; early drought leads to small, shriveled hips.

hi.title: गुलाब: फल विकास एवं विस्तार
hi.shortSummary: गुलाब के विकास का फल विकास एवं विस्तार पड़ाव।
hi.script: कोशिकाओं के तीव्र विस्तार से गुलाब का फल या बीज तेजी से बड़ा होता है, जिसमें जल, शर्करा और पोषक तत्वों का भारी संचय होता है।
hi.script2x: फल या बीज में जल और पोषक तत्वों का भारी संचय होता है और आकार बढ़ता है।
hi.script5x: फल विस्तार: गुलाब का फल या बीज तेजी से पोषण संचित करता है।
hi.visualChanges: गुलाब के आकार और संरचना में स्पष्ट परिवर्तन दिखाई देते हैं।
hi.biologicalProcess: गुलाब की आंतरिक कोशिकाएं इस चरण के विशेष कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।
hi.ecologicalSignificance: यह चरण पौधे की उत्तरजीविता और संतति प्रसार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।
hi.environmentalInfluences: अनुकूल प्रकाश, तापमान और नमी इस चरण को स्वस्थ बनाए रखते हैं।

mr.title: गुलाब: फळाची वाढ व विस्तार
mr.shortSummary: गुलाबच्या वाढीचा फळाची वाढ व विस्तार टप्पा.
mr.script: पेशींच्या वेगामुळे गुलाबचे फळ किंवा दाणे झपाट्याने मोठे होतात आणि त्यात अन्नघटक व पाणी भरू लागते.
mr.script2x: फळामध्ये किंवा दाण्यांमध्ये अन्नद्रव्ये भरून त्यांचा आकार वाढतो.
mr.script5x: फळ वाढ: गुलाबचे फळ किंवा दाणे आकाराने मोठे होतात.
mr.visualChanges: गुलाबच्या रचनेत आणि बाह्य आकारात लक्षणीय बदल दिसून येतात.
mr.biologicalProcess: गुलाबच्या पेशी या टप्प्यातील आवश्यक जैविक क्रिया पूर्ण करतात.
mr.ecologicalSignificance: हा टप्पा वनस्पतीचे अस्तित्व आणि वंशवृद्धी टिकवण्यासाठी अत्यंत महत्त्वाचा आहे.
mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Razungles et al. (1989) Carotenoids and Carotenoid Esters in Rose Hips, Journal of Food Science.

en.title: Rose Hip Color Transition
en.shortSummary: Central hypanthium begins forming vitamin C-rich hip.
en.script: As autumn arrives, the green hypanthium undergoes a rich transformation. Chlorophyll fades as the hip synthesizes lycopene and beta-carotene, shifting from yellowish-orange into a glowing, glossy scarlet berry.
en.script2x: Carotenoids and lycopene accumulate in the hip wall, shifting the color from green to brilliant glossy crimson.
en.script5x: Color Shift: Rose hips turn from green to fiery glossy scarlet.
en.visualChanges: Green hip turns orange and then deep glossy scarlet, holding persistent brown sepals at its tip.
en.biologicalProcess: Massive accumulation of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), carotenoids, and soluble sugars in the fleshy hypanthium wall.
en.ecologicalSignificance: High vitamin C and sugar content make rose hips an indispensable cold-weather survival food for migrating and wintering birds.
en.environmentalInfluences: Cool autumn nights with bright sunny days maximize carotenoid synthesis and fruit sweetness.

hi.title: गुलाब: परिपक्वता व रंग परिवर्तन
hi.shortSummary: गुलाब के विकास का परिपक्वता व रंग परिवर्तन पड़ाव।
hi.script: गुलाब परिपक्वता के अंतिम चरण में पहुँचता है। रंग बदलता है, बीज सख्त होते हैं और फसल संकलन योग्य बनती है।
hi.script2x: रंग परिवर्तन और पोषण संचय से फसल परिपक्व होकर पक जाती है।
hi.script5x: परिपक्वता: गुलाब की फसल पूरी तरह पककर तैयार होती है।
hi.visualChanges: गुलाब के आकार और संरचना में स्पष्ट परिवर्तन दिखाई देते हैं।
hi.biologicalProcess: गुलाब की आंतरिक कोशिकाएं इस चरण के विशेष कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।
hi.ecologicalSignificance: यह चरण पौधे की उत्तरजीविता और संतति प्रसार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।
hi.environmentalInfluences: अनुकूल प्रकाश, तापमान और नमी इस चरण को स्वस्थ बनाए रखते हैं।

mr.title: गुलाब: फळ पिकणे व परिपक्वता
mr.shortSummary: गुलाबच्या वाढीचा फळ पिकणे व परिपक्वता टप्पा.
mr.script: गुलाब पूर्ण पिकण्याच्या टप्प्यावर येतो. नैसर्गिक रंग बदलून दाणे किंवा फळे काढणीसाठी परिपक्व होतात.
mr.script2x: रंग बदलून आणि दाणे भरून पीक काढणीसाठी परिपक्व बनते.
mr.script5x: पीक पिकणे: गुलाबचे पीक पूर्णपणे पक्व होते.
mr.visualChanges: गुलाबच्या रचनेत आणि बाह्य आकारात लक्षणीय बदल दिसून येतात.
mr.biologicalProcess: गुलाबच्या पेशी या टप्प्यातील आवश्यक जैविक क्रिया पूर्ण करतात.
mr.ecologicalSignificance: हा टप्पा वनस्पतीचे अस्तित्व आणि वंशवृद्धी टिकवण्यासाठी अत्यंत महत्त्वाचा आहे.
mr.environmentalInfluences: योग्य सूर्यप्रकाश, तापमान आणि ओलावा या टप्प्यासाठी पोषक ठरतात.

stages.references: Kovacs et al. (2000) Nutritional and Medicinal Value of Rose Hips, Horticultural Science.

en.title: Peak Floral Shrub & Scarlet Hips
en.shortSummary: Stately rose shrub with lush compound canopy and vibrant hips.
en.script: The wild rose stands proudly at the close of the season. Its arching woody canes, adorned with glossy crimson hips, form an enduring sanctuary for wildlife, ready to endure winter storms until spring awakens the cycle anew.
en.script2x: The perennial shrub stands stately with arched canes laden with scarlet hips, prepared for winter dormancy.
en.script5x: Full Maturity: Regal woody shrub laden with glossy crimson hips ready for winter.
en.visualChanges: Mature, stately woody shrub with sprawling prickly canes laden with bright crimson-scarlet rose hips.
en.biologicalProcess: Physiological dormancy sets in; starch reserves are banked in the woody root crown and canes, preparing the shrub for freezing winters.
en.ecologicalSignificance: Perennial architecture ensures year-over-year persistence, providing cover, nesting sites, and winter food for native wildlife.
en.environmentalInfluences: Late-season freezing temperatures soften the hips, making them palatable for winter thrushes and waxwings to disperse seeds.

hi.title: गुलाब: पूर्ण वयस्क परिपक्वता

hi.script2x: पौधा पूर्ण वयस्क है, परिपक्व उपज से लदा हुआ और कटाई के लिए तैयार।
hi.script5x: पूर्ण परिपक्वता: गुलाब की फसल कटाई के लिए तैयार है।
hi.visualChanges: गुलाब के आकार और संरचना में स्पष्ट परिवर्तन दिखाई देते हैं।
hi.biologicalProcess: गुलाब की आंतरिक कोशिकाएं इस चरण के विशेष कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।
hi.ecologicalSignificance: यह चरण पौधे की उत्तरजीविता और संतति प्रसार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।
hi.environmentalInfluences: अनुकूल प्रकाश, तापमान और नमी इस चरण को स्वस्थ बनाए रखते हैं।

mr.script5x: पूर्ण परिपक्वता: गुलाबची भरघोस फसल काढणीसाठी सज्ज आहे.
mr.visualChanges: गुलाबच्या रचनेत आणि बाह्य आकारात लक्षणीय बदल दिसून येतात.
mr.biologicalProcess: गुलाबच्या पेशी या टप्प्यातील आवश्यक जैविक क्रिया पूर्ण करतात.
